words.gram: m. acc. sg., taddhita on a tat-puruṣa

hindi: अब इसलिए हम चिकित्साप्राभृतीय नामक अध्याय की व्याख्या करेंगे।
english: Now, therefore, we shall expound the chapter on the cikitsāprābhṛta (Cikitsāprābhṛtīya).
notes: cikitsāprābhṛta (pra-ā-√bhṛ, prābhṛta 'offering, present') is used in this chapter for the physician who brings treatment (units 3, 12, 37); the literal sense of the compound is not certain. The unit is prose although typed as "verse".

hindi: ऐसा भगवान् आत्रेय ने कहा।
english: Thus said the venerable Ātreya.
notes: The unit is prose although typed as "verse".

hindi: बुद्धिमान्, शास्त्रज्ञ, कर्म में तत्पर चिकित्साप्राभृत जिस मनुष्य का विरेचन करता है, वह सम्यक् योग से सुख पाता है।
english: The man whom the cikitsāprābhṛta, intelligent, versed in the science and devoted to practice, purges obtains happiness through proper application (yoga).

text_flags.why: Missing 't'; the chapter title (unit 1) and units 12, 37 read cikitsāprābhṛta. Probable typo.

notes: yoga here is the proper degree of purgation, contrasted with atiyoga and ayoga in unit 4. 'proper' renders the contrast; the word itself is yoga.

words.gloss: one who fancies himself a physician

hindi: पर जिस मनुष्य का विरेचन अज्ञानी वैद्यमानी करता है, वह मनुष्य अतियोग और अयोग से दुःख पाता है।
english: But the man whom an ignorant one who fancies himself a physician (vaidyamānin) purges, that man obtains suffering from excessive application (atiyoga) and deficient application (ayoga).

text_flags.why: avudha is not a word; tu + abudhaḥ 'ignorant' gives the sense, v for b. Probable typo.

words.gram: f. nom. sg., tat-puruṣa with dvandva first member

hindi: दुर्बलता, लघुता, ग्लानि, व्याधियों की अल्पता, रुचि, हृदय और वर्ण की शुद्धि, भूख-प्यास, समय पर वेगों का प्रवर्तन,
english: Weakness, lightness, languor, lessening of the diseases, relish (for food), purity of heart and complexion, hunger and thirst, the coming on of the urges (vega) at the proper time,
notes: The list continues into unit 6, which ends it with "samyagviriktaliṅgāni" (signs of the properly purged). kṣut-tṛṣṇā is a dvandva in the feminine singular, taking the gender of its last member, not the usual neuter samāhāra form.

words.gloss: purity of intellect, senses and mind
words.gram: f. nom. sg., tat-puruṣa with dvandva first member

words.gloss: of the digestive fire of the body

hindi: बुद्धि, इन्द्रियों और मन की शुद्धि, मारुत की अनुलोमता और कायाग्नि का अनुवर्तन — ये सम्यक् विरिक्त के लक्षण हैं।
english: purity of intellect, senses and mind, downward movement of Vāta (māruta), and the normal functioning of the digestive fire of the body: these are the signs of one properly purged.
notes: Ends the list begun in unit 5. buddhīndriya may also be read as one term, 'the cognitive sense faculties', giving 'purity of the cognitive senses and the mind'. anuvartana literally 'following, continuing'.

hindi: थूकना, हृदय की अशुद्धि, श्लेष्मा और पित्त का उत्क्लेश, आध्मान, अरुचि, छर्दि, दुर्बलता का न होना, लघुता का न होना,
english: Spitting, impurity of the heart, nausea (utkleśa) of Kapha (śleṣman) and Pitta, distension, loss of taste, vomiting, absence of weakness, absence of lightness,

text_flags.why: chirdi is not a word; chardi 'vomiting' fits the list of signs. Probable typo.

notes: The list continues into unit 8, which ends it with "lakṣaṇāny aviriktānām" (signs of the unpurged).

words.gram: n. nom. sg., tat-puruṣa with dvandva first member

hindi: जाँघों और ऊरुओं में शिथिलता, तन्द्रा, स्तैमित्य, पीनस का आना और मारुत का रुकना — ये अविरिक्तों के लक्षण हैं।
english: weariness of the shanks and thighs, drowsiness, staimitya (stiffness), onset of pīnasa, and suppression of Vāta (māruta): these are the signs of the unpurged.
notes: Ends the list begun in unit 7. sadana 'sinking, weariness'. pīnasa and staimitya kept as Sanskrit.

words.gloss: of faeces, Pitta, Kapha and Vāta
resembling water of fat and flesh

hindi: मल, पित्त, कफ और वात के क्रम से निकल आने के बाद जो रक्त बहता है, जो मेद और मांस के जल के समान हो,
english: When faeces, Pitta, Kapha and Vāta have come out in sequence, the blood that flows after that, resembling water of fat and flesh,
notes: The sentence continues into unit 10, which ends "so 'tiyogaḥ". medomāṃsodakopamam may also be read 'resembling fat, flesh or water'. viṭ is the stem viś 'faeces' in compound.

words.gram: pres. part. pra-√muh, m. gen. sg.

hindi: या श्लेष्मा और पित्त से रहित जल, या काला रक्त — प्यासे, मारुत से पीड़ित और मूर्च्छित होते हुए मनुष्य का वह अतियोग है।
english: or water free of Kapha (śleṣman) and Pitta, or black blood, in one who is thirsty, afflicted by Vāta (māruta) and fainting: that is excessive application (atiyoga).
notes: Ends the sentence begun in unit 9. The 'or' of the first item is supplied from vā; the items are alternatives for what flows after the doṣas.

hindi: क्योंकि वमन के अधिक किए जाने पर ये वही लक्षण होते हैं; और ऊपर जाने वाले वातरोग तथा अतिरिक्त रूप से वाग्ग्रह हो सकता है।
english: For when emesis is overdone these same signs occur; and upward-moving Vāta diseases and, in addition, obstruction of speech may occur.
notes: adhikaḥ agrees with vāggrahaḥ; it may also mean 'in excess' ('excessive obstruction of speech').

hindi: इसलिए मनुष्य उस चिकित्साप्राभृत की शरण में जाए, जो उसे अत्यन्त आयु और सुख से युक्त करे।
english: Therefore a man should approach as refuge the cikitsāprābhṛta who would join him to the utmost with life and with happiness.

hindi: अविपाक, अरुचि, स्थूलता, पाण्डुता, भारीपन, क्लम, पिडका, कोठ और कण्डू की उत्पत्ति और अरति,
english: Indigestion, loss of taste, obesity, pallor, heaviness, exhaustion, the arising of pimples (piḍakā), koṭha and itching, and discontent (arati),
notes: The list of signs of one with much doṣa runs through units 13 to 16. koṭha kept as Sanskrit. The dvandva takes the gender of its last member (kaṇḍū, f.).

words.gram: m. nom. sg., tat-puruṣa with dvandva first member

hindi: आलस्य, श्रम और दुर्बलता, दुर्गन्ध, अवसादक, श्लेष्मा और पित्त का समुत्क्लेश, नींद का नाश, अतिनिद्रा,
english: laziness, fatigue and weakness, foul smell, lassitude (avasādaka), agitation (samutkleśa) of Kapha (śleṣman) and Pitta, loss of sleep, excessive sleep,
notes: avasādaka as a masculine noun 'lassitude, sinking' is uncommon (avasāda is the usual noun); the sense is clear.

words.gram: m. nom. sg., tat-puruṣa with dvandva first member

hindi: तन्द्रा, क्लीबता, बुद्धिहीनता, अशुभ स्वप्नों का दिखना, और बृंहण उपायों के होते हुए भी प्यासे मनुष्य के बल और वर्ण का नाश,
english: drowsiness, impotence, lack of intellect, seeing inauspicious dreams, and loss of strength and complexion in one who is thirsty, even with nourishing measures,

text_flags.why: possible: tṛṣyataḥ 'of one thirsting' sits awkwardly with the instrumental bṛṃhaṇair api; √tṛp 'be satisfied' takes the instrumental, giving 'even in one satisfied with nourishing measures'. Translation follows the printed text.

notes: The construction of tṛṣyataḥ with bṛṃhaṇair api is unclear as printed; see text_flags.

hindi: — ये बहुदोष वाले के लक्षण हैं। उसके लिए दोष के अनुसार और बल के अनुसार ऊर्ध्व और अनुलोम संशोधन हितकर है।
english: these are the signs of one with much doṣa. For him purification, both upward and downward, according to the doṣa and according to strength, is beneficial.
notes: Ends the list begun in unit 13. ūrdhvam and anulomam agree with saṃśodhanam (emesis and purgation).

words.gloss: of one whose bowel is purified

hindi: इस प्रकार जिसका कोष्ठ विशुद्ध हो गया है, उसकी कायाग्नि बढ़ती है, व्याधियाँ शान्त होती हैं और प्रकृति बनी रहती है।
english: Thus, in one whose bowel (koṣṭha) is purified the digestive fire of the body increases, the diseases subside and the normal state (prakṛti) continues.

hindi: उसकी इन्द्रियाँ, मन-बुद्धि और वर्ण प्रसन्न होते हैं; और उसमें बल, पुष्टि, सन्तान और वृषता उत्पन्न होती है।
english: His senses, mind and intellect, and complexion become clear; and strength, nourishment, offspring and virility arise in him.
notes: manobuddhiḥ is taken as a dvandva in the feminine singular (gender of its last member), not the neuter samāhāra form; it may also be a tat-puruṣa 'the intellect of the mind'. The singular verbs prasīdati and jāyate agree with the nearest subject.

hindi: वह कठिनाई से बुढ़ापा पाता है और रोगरहित होकर देर तक जीता है। इसलिए मनुष्य उचित समय पर युक्ति से युक्त संशोधन पिए।
english: He reaches old age with difficulty and, free from disease, lives long. Therefore a man should drink purification at the proper time, applied with rational planning (yukti).

hindi: लंघन और पाचन से जीते गए दोष कभी-कभी कुपित हो जाते हैं; पर जो संशोधन से जीते गए हैं, उनका फिर से उद्भव नहीं होता।
english: Doṣas subdued by lightening and digesting measures sometimes become aggravated; but those that are subdued by purifications do not arise again.
notes: Last clause literally 'there is no re-arising of them'.

hindi: दोषों और वृक्षों की जड़ के नष्ट न होने पर, गए हुए रोगों और अंकुरों का लौटना निश्चित है।
english: With doṣas and with trees, when the root is not destroyed, the return of diseases and of shoots that have gone is certain.

text_flags.why: possible omission: the line has 15 syllables, one short of the 16 of the other half-verses, and the parallel first line pairs its genitives with ca ... ca.

notes: Construction is in loc. absolute (mūle 'nupahate sati). The 'and' between rogāṇām and prasavānām is supplied; see text_flags.

words.gloss: accompanied by ghee, meat-juice, milk and pleasing yūṣa
words.gram: m. inst. pl., tat-puruṣa with dvandva first member

hindi: औषध से क्षीण हुए मनुष्य में आहारों से ही बृंहण हितकर है, जो घी, मांसरस, दूध और हृद्य यूष से युक्त हों,
english: In one wasted by medicine, nourishing by foods alone is wholesome, foods accompanied by ghee, meat-juice, milk and pleasing yūṣa,

text_flags.why: kṣapita (ppp. of caus. √kṣi, 'wasted') has one t; kṣapitta is not a form. Probable typo; metre is unaffected.

notes: The sentence continues into unit 23. hṛdya 'pleasing to the heart' may qualify yūṣa only or the whole list. yūṣa kept as Sanskrit.

words.gloss: by oil massage and rubbing with unguents

hindi: और अभ्यङ्ग, उत्सादन, स्नानों तथा अनुवासन सहित निरूहों से; इस प्रकार वह कल्याण पाता है और देर तक आयु से युक्त रहता है।
english: and by oil massage, rubbing with unguents, baths, and decoction enemas together with unctuous enemas; thus he obtains well-being and is joined with life for long.
notes: Continues unit 22. The 'and' at the start is supplied to link the instrumentals with those of unit 22.

words.gloss: for those afflicted by excessive application

hindi: अतियोग से ग्रस्त लोगों के लिए घी का पान प्रशंसित है, मधुरक द्रव्यों से सिद्ध तेल या फिर अनुवासन।
english: For those afflicted by excessive application (atiyoga), the drinking of ghee is praised, or oil prepared with sweet drugs (madhuraka), or else an unctuous enema.
notes: anubaddha literally 'bound up with, attended by'. It is not certain whether tailam ... siddham is a separate remedy or the substance of the anuvāsana ('or an unctuous enema of oil prepared with sweet drugs').

words.gloss: taking account of measure, time and strength
words.gram: m. nom. sg., upapada tat-puruṣa with dvandva first member

hindi: पर जिसका अयोग हुआ हो, उस मनुष्य का स्नेहन करके, मात्रा, काल और बल का ध्यान रखते हुए तथा पिछले क्रम को याद रखते हुए, फिर से संशोधन करे।
english: But one in whom there is deficient application (ayoga), that man, once oleated, one should purify again, taking account of measure, time and strength, and remembering the previous sequence.
notes: snigdham is predicative ('when oleated'); the agent of saṃśodhayet is not named. pūrvam may also be adverbial ('the sequence as before').

words.gram: ppp. vi-√dhā, n. loc. sg., tat-puruṣa

hindi: स्नेहन, स्वेदन, शुद्धि और संसर्जन के अनुचित रीति से किए जाने पर जो रोग उत्पन्न होते हैं, उनका साधन सिद्धियों में है।
english: The diseases that arise when oleation, sweating, purification and the graduated diet (saṃsarjana) are done improperly: the means of their cure is in the Siddhis.
notes: a-mārga-vihite literally 'done by a wrong path'; it is loc. sg. and refers to each of the four procedures. siddhiṣu 'in the successes' probably refers to the later treatment of success (siddhi) in therapy, i.e. the Siddhi section; this is an interpretation.

hindi: कारणों की विषमता से शरीर की धातुएँ विषम हो जाती हैं और कारणों की समता से सम; उनका स्वभाव से उपरम सदा होता है।
english: From imbalance of causes the dhātus of the body become unbalanced, from balance of causes balanced; their cessation by their own nature (svabhāvoparama) is constant.
notes: svabhāvoparama: things cease by their own nature, without a cause of cessation (taken up in unit 28).

hindi: भावों की प्रवृत्ति का कारण होता है, उनके निरोध में कारण नहीं है; कुछ लोग वहाँ भी कारण के न रहने को कारण मानते हैं।
english: There is a cause for the arising of entities; for their cessation there is no cause. Some think that even there the non-continuation of the cause is the cause.
notes: The first clause has no verb; 'there is' is supplied from asti of the second clause.

hindi: जिस आचार्य ने इस प्रकार विषय कहा था, उनसे अग्निवेश बोले — स्वभाव से उपरम होने पर चिकित्साप्राभृत का कर्म क्या है?
english: To the teacher who had thus stated the matter, Agniveśa said: "If cessation is by nature, what is the action of the cikitsāprābhṛta?

text_flags.why: Transposed letters; the chapter's term is cikitsāprābhṛta (units 1, 12, 37). Probable typo.

notes: Agniveśa's question continues into unit 30.

hindi: भिषक् औषधों से किन विषम धातुओं को सम करता है? या, हे भगवन्, चिकित्सा क्या है, या वह किस प्रयोजन से प्रयुक्त की जाती है?
english: Which unbalanced dhātus does the physician make balanced with medicines? Or what is treatment, O venerable one, or for what purpose is it applied?"
notes: Ends Agniveśa's question begun in unit 29.

hindi: शिष्य का वह वचन सुनकर पुनर्वसु बोले — हे सौम्य, इस विषय में महर्षियों ने जो युक्ति देखी है, वह सुनो।
english: Having heard that word of the disciple, Punarvasu spoke: "Hear, gentle one, the reasoning (yukti) on this that has been seen by the great sages.

text_flags.why: tat + śiṣya gives tacchiṣya; 'ticch' has no grammatical source. Probable typo; metre is unaffected.

notes: somya is a common short form of the vocative saumya and is not flagged. śrūyatām literally 'let it be heard'. Punarvasu's answer continues to unit 38.

words.gloss: because of the absence of a cause of destruction

hindi: नाश के कारण के अभाव से भावों के नाश का कारण नहीं जाना जाता, जैसे सदा चलने वाले काल के बीतने का कारण।
english: Because there is no cause of destruction, the cause of the destruction of entities is not known, as with the cause of the passing of ever-moving time.
notes: The sentence is compressed; na may also be taken with the ablative: 'It is not for want of a cause of destruction (that things endure); the cause of destruction of entities is not perceived, like that of ever-moving time.' The two readings give different sense.

hindi: शीघ्र गति के कारण भाव जैसे उत्पन्न हुआ है, वैसे नष्ट हो जाता है; उसके निरोध में कोई कारण नहीं है, और न अन्यथा करना।
english: Because of its swift going, as an entity has come into being, so it perishes; for its cessation there is no cause, nor any acting otherwise.
notes: śīghragatva 'swiftness' is formed with -tva on śīghraga 'swift-going'. yathā bhūtaḥ may also be read 'just as it has come about'. anyathākriyā 'altering (the course)' is a possible sense.

hindi: जिन क्रियाओं से शरीर में धातुएँ सम हो जाती हैं, वह विकारों की चिकित्सा है; वह भिषकों का कर्म माना गया है।
english: The actions by which the dhātus in the body become balanced, that is the treatment of disorders; that is held to be the action of physicians.

hindi: 'शरीर में धातुओं की विषमता कैसे न हो और सम धातुओं का अनुबन्ध कैसे बना रहे' — इस प्रयोजन से क्रिया की जाती है।
english: "How may there be no imbalance of the dhātus in the body, and continuance of the balanced ones?": for this purpose action is performed.
notes: katham governs both clauses; the second is 'and (how) may there be continuance of the balanced ones'.

hindi: विषम कारणों के त्याग से और सम कारणों के सेवन से विषम धातुएँ बनी नहीं रहतीं, धातुएँ सम हो जाती हैं।
english: By giving up the causes of imbalance and by using balanced ones, the unbalanced (dhātus) do not persist; the dhātus become balanced.
notes: viṣamahetu literally 'unbalanced causes'. samānām refers to balanced causes. viṣamāḥ refers to the dhātus.

hindi: क्योंकि वह सम कारणों से सम धातुओं को उत्पन्न करता है, इसलिए चिकित्साप्राभृत देह, सुख और आयु का दाता है।
english: Since by balanced causes he would produce balanced dhātus, therefore the cikitsāprābhṛta is the giver of body, happiness and life.

text_flags.why: The acc. pl. of dhātu is dhātūn (as in unit 30); short u is a probable typo.

notes: tu here marks the next step of the argument; rendered by the sentence order. deha-sukha-āyuṣām may also be read 'of bodily happiness and life'.

hindi: देह, सुख और आयु के दान से वैद्य धर्म, अर्थ, काम और दोनों नरलोकों का दाता बन जाता है।
english: By the giving of body, happiness and life, the physician becomes the giver of dharma, wealth (artha), pleasure (kāma), and of both worlds of men.
notes: nṛlokasya ubhayasya literally 'of the world of men, of both'; ubhaya is commonly understood as this world and the next, an interpretation not stated in the line.

words.gloss: of proper, deficient and excessive application

hindi: यहाँ श्लोक हैं — चिकित्साप्राभृत का गुण और जो दोष दूसरे में रहता है, शुद्धि से सम्बन्धित योग, अयोग और अतियोग का लक्षण,
english: Here, the verses: the quality of the cikitsāprābhṛta, and the fault that rests in the other; the sign of proper, deficient and excessive application (yoga, ayoga, atiyoga) relating to purification;
notes: The summary continues to unit 41. 'the other' (itara) is the one who fancies himself a physician (unit 4); the line does not name him.

words.gloss: relating to success and ill effects
words.gram: n. nom. sg., bahuvrīhi with dvandva first member

hindi: बहुदोष वाले के लक्षण और संशोधन के जो गुण हैं, और सिद्धि तथा व्यापत्ति से सम्बन्धित चिकित्सा का सूत्रमात्र,
english: the signs of one with much doṣa, and the qualities of purification; and the bare outline of treatment relating to success and ill effects;

text_flags.why: possible: the noun from vi-ā-√pad is vyāpatti (or vyāpad); vyāpati with one t is irregular. Metre is unaffected.

notes: sūtramātra 'mere thread', i.e. a brief outline; this refers to unit 26.

hindi: और चिकित्सा में जो युक्ति है तथा भिषक् जो प्रयोजन सिद्ध करता है — वह सब मुनि ने चिकित्साप्राभृत अध्याय में कहा।
english: and what reasoning (yukti) there is in treatment, and what purpose the physician accomplishes: all that the sage stated in the chapter on the cikitsāprābhṛta.
notes: Ends the summary begun in unit 39. The chapter is referred to by the bare compound cikitsāprābhṛta, not by its title form Cikitsāprābhṛtīya.

hindi: अग्निवेश द्वारा रचित, चरक द्वारा प्रतिसंस्कृत तन्त्र में, श्लोकस्थान में चिकित्साप्राभृतीय नामक सोलहवाँ अध्याय।
english: In the treatise composed by Agniveśa and redacted by Caraka, in the Ślokasthāna, the sixteenth chapter named Cikitsāprābhṛtīya.

text_flags.why: The avagraha of ṣoḍaśo 'dhyāyaḥ (ṣoḍaśaḥ + adhyāyaḥ) is missing; dhyāya alone is not a word. Probable typo.

notes: Chapter colophon.

hindi: कल्पनाचतुष्क पूर्ण।
english: The tetrad on preparation (kalpanā): completed.
notes: Closes the group of four chapters (catuṣka) named after kalpanā; the chapters are not named in this line.
